title: Dodds, joining King Oliver, Ory on trombone
summary: Nicholas recalls Dodds around 1912, then taking his place in Oliver's band in 1924; trombonists George Filhe and Ory.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: No, when I met Johnny, he was playing. He was playing his head off around 1912. At Betsy Cole. No, Ms. Cole's Lauren. I don't know. We used to say Ms. Cole's Lauren. It used to be penny parties on Sundays, you know, for the youngsters, you know. I was a kid, twelve years old, and I used to go up there. And I was learning time and time, and he was respiring quite a bit. And Johnny was up. And then, of course, I met him to the years. She called. I took his place. And King Howard was playing in 24. When they left the band, he wasn't playing sax. And I was playing sax, and so King sent for Bonnie and myself, Paul, Bob, Rimmie, and Wistler. And I got to know him real well.
Mm-hmm. Did the... When you first joined Oliver, who was the trombone player? George Fields. George Fields. George Fields.
Yeah, old George Fields. He was dead, I think. Mm-hmm. Then we sent and got Ori in California. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm.
What did Ori play then? He played trombone.
Yeah. He sent and got him and came to Chicago.
